text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Prime Minister Gyula Horn said that the administration had reached a turning point, and phenomena are emerging in society which prove that the first phase of the change of regime has ended, and that will determine the legal, political and legislative tasks of the forthcoming period.
- Both the Socialist and Free Democrat parties confirmed their commitment to the coalition in separate meetings at the weekend.
- New York Governor George Pataki laid the foundation stone yesterday at a meat plant in the village of Aranyosapati, his grandparents' homeland. Today he is due to meet President Arpad Goncz.

- An investigation by the State Audit Office is looking into the 1993 GSM tender for concession rights for digital telephone services to discover why the contract was transferred from Transelektro to Technoimpex.
- Free Democrat President Ivan Peto told a party commemoration in the Corvin Cinema on Sunday that the 1956 Uprising is one of the purest chapters of Hungarian history.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- In an interview with Reuters, the European Union Ambassador to Budapest Hans Beck said on Friday it is an illusion to believe that Central European countries can join the European Union before 2002. (Sat.)
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn, Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky and Slovak Premier Vladimir Meciar will hold their forthcoming summit in Posteny, Slovakia on November 4. (Sat.)
- General George Joulwan, commander-in-chief of NATO's European forces, begins a two-day visit to Budapest today. (Sat.)
- The draft 1997 budget, which Parliament begins debating tomorrow, projects a deficit of HUF 301.7 billion for the year.
- Two Canadian IFOR soldiers are facing charges after they and two other persons reportedly stopped a car in Buda Friday night, injured the driver and molested a female passenger.
NEPSZABADSAG

- Marta Tocsik, the woman at the centre of the privatisation scandal, said on television Sunday that she is prepared to reduce the HUF 804 million she was paid by the State Privatisation and Holding Co. (APV) provided her sub-contractors and APV comply.
- The heads of the European Socialist parties will hold a summit in Budapest October 26-27.
NEPSZAVA
- Heart surgeries will stop at the Imre Haynal University of Health Science heart clinic as of today for lack of medical instruments.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Convertible currency revenues from tourism in the first eight months of this year totalled $1.5 billion.
- Exports from industrial duty-free zones in Hungary totalled $1.58 billion while imports reached $1.45 billion in the first eight months of the year.
- The State Debt Management Centre will issue two state bonds on October 31. (Sat.)
- TVK is planning to transform its plastic processing branches into independent companies and may offer minority stakes to professional investors.
- The British store chain Tesco will open its first Budapest outlet in the Polus shopping centre on November 8.
- Creditanstalt Rt. has opened a new branch in Szombathely.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
